title: Keystone Pilot Readiness: Acceptance Gates, Observability Signals, and Support Escalation Ladder
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Objective: Prepare a gated launch playbook for the first cohort of Keystone (high-commitment) pilot customers. Deliver a pragmatic acceptance matrix, observability signal definitions, and a stepped support/escalation ladder so Engineering, Support, and Customer Success can operate confidently during beta-to-production transitions. Scope excludes full GA pricing and marketing copy; this ticket covers operational readiness, release note coordination, and post-pilot rollback / remediation runbooks.
success_criteria: All Keystone pilots have a signed readiness checklist signed-off by PM, Eng, and CS before canary traffic (5 customers in cohort 1)
Telemetry dashboard surfaces P50/P95 latency, error rate, quality-regression score, and cost-per-token within 1 hour of deployment
Support runbook validated by a staged tabletop exercise and assigned to on-call rota
Release notes sent to customers and account teams 48 hours before canary with clear rollback criteria and expected SLOs
No customer-facing incidents with severity >= Sev2 during first 72 hours of canary; any regressions have <24h remediation plan
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Preflight (T-14 to T-7): finalize acceptance matrix, handbooks, and release notes; dry-run alerting and escalation
Phase 1 - Canary (T0 to T+3): route 5% of customer requests from 3 Keystone accounts; monitor critical signals; freeze config changes
Phase 2 - Incremental Increase (T+4 to T+14): expand to full pilot cohort if no critical regressions; begin weekly satisfaction surveys
Phase 3 - Production Handoff (T+15): transition to Dedicated/GA path, capture post-mortem and improvement backlog
release_notes_coordination: PM drafts customer-facing release note (summary, expected changes, known limitations, rollback criteria)
Engineering provides bullet list of behavioral changes, API schema diffs, and mitigations for breaking changes
Design/Docs owner validates examples and migration steps; legal reviews security language where required
Send release note to account teams + customers 48 hours prior; include support contact and escalation ladder
feedback_flow: In-product feedback widget collected to a central pilot Slack channel (#pilot-keystone-feedback)
Weekly triage with CS, Eng, and PM to convert signals into action items (deploy fixes, prompt set updates, docs)
Dedicated Google Sheet for qualitative feedback mapped to feature areas and account priority
Set up NPS-lite survey at Day 7 and Day 21 post-canary for each participant
telemetry_signals: Success rate: 2xx vs 5xx/4xx by route and model variant
Quality regression metric: baseline prompt evaluation score and human-sampled error rate
Cost signals: tokens per request, cost-per-call and cost-per-customer-hour
Operational signals: queue depth, batch sizes, kernel fallbacks, KV cache hit rate
dependencies: ENG-21892: Runtime canary routing by account
ENG-22311: Telemetry pipeline: real-time aggregation for pilot metrics
ENG-22900: Support tool integration (Zendesk <> Slack) for pilot channel
DES-1847: Release note template and canonical examples
risks: Quality regression undetected by automated evals due to narrow prompt coverage
Telemetry alert noise leading to operator fatigue and missed degradations
Customer-specific prompts cause unexpected cost spikes
Escalation confusion across Timezones leading to slow remediation
mitigation_actions: Expand eval prompt set with account-specific examples prior to canary
Tune alert thresholds and add a 'pilot-only' alarm suppression window during non-business hours
Set per-account cost caps for first 7 days of canary and telemetry cost dashboards
Define primary/secondary on-call for each region and publish escalation phone matrix
